decision_titles: Jurisdiction over trespassing and unauthorized activity allegations
Complaint filed by Rene Marro and Beth Marro
plain_text:
Board of Ethics  
Draft Meeting Minutes 
Thursday, November 12, 2026 
City Council Chambers 
37 Green Street 
9:30 AM 
 
 
1. Call to Order 
Chair Sullivan called the meeting to order at 9:31 a.m. 
2. Roll Call 
Present: John Sullivan, Stephen Shurtleff, Tenley Callaghan, Adam Pignatelli 
Staff Present- City Solicitor John Conforti  
Not Present: James Rosenberg, Marcia Moran 
3. Approval of the Draft Meeting Minutes 
Mr. Shurleff moved approval of the draft minutes for the February 27, 2026 meeting.  The 
motion was duly seconded by Ms. Callaghan. The motion passed with Mr. Pignatelli 
abstaining. 
4. Consideration of the Complaint filed by Rene Marro and Beth Marro 
Chair Sullivan stated that the members of the Board had reviewed the complaint and th e 
response submitted by Mr. Andrew Gould . He explained that, following receipt of the 
complaint, he had spoken with the City Solicitor and reviewed the Board’s rules.  He provided 
members with an excerpt from the Board’s rules and an excerpt from the City of Concord’s 
Code of Ethics, and explained the Board would need to determine whether the complaint, as 
submitted, merits the scheduling of a public hearing. 
 
The Board discussed the scope of its jurisdiction and authority regarding the complaint, noting 
that its role is limited to reviewing alleged conflicts of interest and making recommendations 
to the City Council. The Board determined that allegations concerning unauthorized activities 
or possible trespassing on City property fall outside its jurisdiction and are more appropriately 
addressed by the City Council or City Manager. However, the Board recognized that the
complaint also appeared to raise a potential conflict-of-interest concern regarding Mr. Gould’s 
service on the Trail Subcommittee and his involvement with another organization. 
 
The Board reviewed the applicable conflict -of-interest definition, including provisions 
addressing circumstances in which an official or a family member may receive a direct or 
indirect financial benefit through actions taken in an official capacity or through an association 
with another organization. Members discussed whether Mr. Gould’s simultaneous service on 
a municipal board and the governing body of another organization could constitute a conflict 
of interest. Discussion focused on whether the provisi on requires evidence of an actual or 
potential financial benefit to the individual or the outside organization. Based on the 
information provided, members expressed concern that the complaint did not establish a 
financial interest or benefit resulting from Mr. Gould’s actions. 
 
Ms. Callaghan moved to dismiss the complaint without a vote.  The motion was duly seconded 
by Mr. Shurtleff and passed by a unanimous vote. 
 
5. Setting of Future Meeting Dates, if applicable 
City Solicitor Conforti noted there was nothing pending at this time, however, the City Council 
will be considering amendments to the Ethics Ordinance in December. He stated depending on 
the outcome, the Board may wish to schedule a group discussion regarding the changes, either 
before it’s next  hearing or during a non -meeting, attorney -client session. He encouraged 
members of the Board to review the proposed amendments and City Council actions in 
December. 
6. Adjournment 
Ms. Callaghan moved to adjourn the meeting at 9:41 a.m.  The motion was duly s econded by 
Mr. Shurtleff and passed by a unanimous vote. 
A true copy; I attest:  
Deborah Tuite  
Deputy City Clerk 
This meeting is open to the public although there is no public input or testimony.
